title: Trading Strategy Optimization via Textual Gradient
summary: Quantitative trading strategy design aims to discover trading programs from historical data that remain effective in future markets, which can be viewed as a black-box program optimization problem. LLM-based textual gradients offer a promising approach by providing explicit optimization directions for iterative strategy refinement. However, directly applying textual gradients faces two challenges: (1) optimization is myopic, underutilizing experience from previous evaluations; and (2) aggregate backtest feedback overlooks temporal robustness, potentially favoring strategies that perform well only in specific market periods. To address these challenges, we propose TradeGrad, an experience-guided textual-gradient framework for robust trading strategy optimization. TradeGrad leverages accumulated optimization experience to estimate textual gradients and employs multi-scale revisions for both strategy exploration and refinement. It further introduces the Cross-Period Robust Objective (CPRO), which emphasizes performance in unfavorable historical periods to promote temporal robustness. Experiments on cross-sectional and time-series strategy design in Chinese A-share and U.S. equity markets show that TradeGrad achieves the best in-sample and out-of-sample performance across all four settings. Notably, its Chinese cross-sectional strategy achieves 27.99% annualized return, 12.19% maximum drawdown, and a Sharpe ratio of 1.63, approximately 68% higher than the CSI 300 benchmark. Further analyses validate the proposed components and show consistent improvements in both in-sample and out-of-sample performance throughout optimization. The code is available at https://github.com/transcend-0/TradeGrad.
core_methodology: TradeGrad utilizes LLM-based textual gradients for trading strategy optimization, incorporating experience-guided optimization and multi-scale revisions. It introduces the Cross-Period Robust Objective (CPRO) to enhance temporal robustness by focusing on performance in unfavorable historical periods.
data_sources: Chinese A-share and U.S. equity markets
alpha_potential: The framework demonstrates significant alpha potential through its ability to generate robust trading strategies that perform well both in-sample and out-of-sample, as evidenced by the high annualized return (27.99%) and Sharpe ratio (1.63) in Chinese markets.
title_cn: 通过文本梯度优化交易策略
summary_cn: TradeGrad是一个基于LLM文本梯度的交易策略优化框架，通过经验引导和跨周期鲁棒目标（CPRO）提升策略的时域鲁棒性。在中美股市测试中，其中国横向策略年化收益达27.99%，最大回撤12.19%，夏普比率1.63，显著优于基准。该框架特别注重不利历史时期的策略表现，实现了样本内外一致优化效果。

title: MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code
summary: Large language models are moving from producing trading signals to writing the code that executes them. The failure mode of the second role is silent: generated code runs, a backtest plots, yet the risk logic that the trader described is not the logic being executed. Existing code benchmarks test functional correctness on unit tests and finance benchmarks test forecasting; neither measures whether an implementation behaves like the strategy that was asked for. We introduce MintEval, a benchmark in which reference strategies are generated programmatically from a library of composable building blocks, back-translated into colloquial trader instructions, and re-implemented by the model under test. Generated and reference programs are executed bar by bar on identical market data and frictions, and compared on their actions rather than on code similarity or profit: alpha is differenced away. MintEval v0 contains 800 tasks on BTCUSDT 15-minute data, stratified by an execution-measured state-span complexity tau that is decoupled from description length. Low-cost models reach a mean ActionMatch of at most 0.544 and reproduce at most 0.087 of tasks exactly; on a stratified subset of 200 tasks a frontier model (Claude Opus 5.5) reaches 0.889 and reproduces 0.575 exactly, yet still fails silently on 0.275 of tasks. Given a menu of building blocks, models identify the strategy almost perfectly, yet 79.2% of the implementations whose specification was read correctly diverge on more than 10% of active bars. The LLM judge of a recent strategy-generation benchmark, applied verbatim, accepts every one of these silent failures.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MintEval, a benchmark that evaluates whether LLM-generated trading strategy code correctly implements the specified strategy by comparing the behavior of generated and reference programs on identical market data. It uses a library of composable building blocks to create reference strategies, back-translates these into trader instructions, and tests LLM re-implementations for behavioral equivalence.
data_sources: BTCUSDT 15-minute data is used in MintEval v0, which contains 800 tasks stratified by execution-measured state-span complexity.
alpha_potential: The benchmark itself doesn't generate alpha but provides a critical tool for ensuring LLM-generated trading strategies correctly implement intended logic, reducing silent failures that could lead to significant trading losses.
title_cn: MintEval：LLM是否执行了您要求的交易策略？自然语言到策略代码的行为等效基准
summary_cn: 本文提出MintEval基准测试，通过比较LLM生成的交易策略代码与参考策略在相同市场数据下的行为表现，评估LLM是否准确实现了指定策略。研究发现当前模型存在严重静默错误问题，该工具对量化交易中确保策略实现准确性至关重要。

title: Time Series Forecasting Benchmarks Need Scenario-Grounded Stress Testing
summary: Time series forecasting (TSF) increasingly drives decisions in transportation, energy, finance, healthcare, and infrastructure, yet current evaluation remains overly narrow: standard benchmarks reward low held-out error, while robustness studies typically reduce failure to Gaussian noise, random masking, or bounded adversarial perturbations. This obscures the real failure modes of deployed forecasting systems. Input-side anomalies are not merely noisier inputs: they often reflect structured events that alter temporal dynamics, break cross-variable dependencies, induce regime shifts, or propagate from faulty sensors to downstream decisions. These semantic, causal, and system-level failures cannot be faithfully captured by i.i.d. perturbations alone. The rise of TSF foundation models makes this evaluation gap more urgent, as unauditable pretraining corpora make held-out generalization increasingly unreliable. We therefore advocate scenario-grounded stress testing. Each test instance should include historical inputs and future targets, together with a semantic scenario, an explicit failure operator, and a measurable difficulty level. This shift makes evaluation interpretable, attributable, and deployment-relevant and friendly, enabling the community to ask not only which model is accurate, but under what conditions it fails and why.
core_methodology: Proposes scenario-grounded stress testing for time series forecasting models by incorporating structured semantic scenarios, explicit failure operators, and measurable difficulty levels. Moves beyond traditional Gaussian noise/random masking evaluations to test for real-world regime shifts and causal anomalies.
data_sources: Generic time series data (explicitly applicable to financial time series), with emphasis on handling input-side anomalies reflecting structural market events
alpha_potential: High potential for detecting regime shifts and structural breaks in financial markets - critical for momentum strategies, volatility targeting, and risk management. The framework could systematically identify when forecasting models fail during market crises or structural changes.
title_cn: 时间序列预测基准需要进行情境验证的压力测试
summary_cn: 该论文提出的情境验证压力测试框架专门评估预测模型在市场异常(如结构突变、依赖关系断裂等非高斯扰动)下的表现，对于量化交易的策略鲁棒性测试和风控系统升级具有直接价值。可应用于动量策略失效预警、市场状态识别等场景。

title: Forecasting from Counterfactual Simulator Rollouts: A Sim2Real Evaluation
summary: Deploying a new decision policy creates a cold-start problem for prediction models whose targets depend on the policy's actions: historical observations reflect earlier policies, while real observations under the new policy are not yet available. Simulation offers a way to address this gap by rolling out the target policy across counterfactual scenarios and using the resulting trajectories to learn how the system responds to those controls. The simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) transfer of this simulator-trained model can then be backtested by evaluating it against real observations from past deployments. Using two real-world inventory-control deployments, we evaluate this process from three angles: simulator fidelity, zero-shot transfer to real behavior, and adaptation as real target-policy observations accumulate. The simulator-trained forecaster achieves lower point-estimate mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) than the same architecture trained on historical real data, reducing MAPE by 1.2-3.1 percentage points in Study 1 and 12.5-18.7 points in Study 2. After deployment, lightweight calibration using early real observations further reduces error by up to 2.5 percentage points. These results provide empirical evidence that simulator-generated counterfactual data can support cold-start forecasting under a new policy, and the resulting model can be further refined as real deployment data become available.
core_methodology: This paper employs a novel simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) transfer learning approach where counterfactual simulations of new decision policies are used to generate synthetic training data for forecasting models. The methodology involves: 1) Generating counterfactual rollout trajectories from a simulator, 2) Training prediction models on this synthetic data, 3) Performing zero-shot transfer to real-world deployment, and 4) Subsequent calibration with real observations.
data_sources: The study uses real-world inventory control systems (implicitly containing time-series data of product demands and inventory levels) along with their corresponding simulators that can generate synthetic counterfactual rollout trajectories under different decision policies.
alpha_potential: The approach addresses a fundamental cold-start problem when deploying new trading strategies: historical data reflects old strategies while new strategy data isn't yet available. The demonstrated ability to outperform purely data-trained models (12.5-18.7 percentage point MAPE improvements) suggests potential for generating superior trade execution or portfolio management policies by first thoroughly testing and optimizing them in simulation before real deployment.
title_cn: 基于反事实模拟轨迹的预测方法：一项仿真到现实的评估研究
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种创新方法，通过模拟器生成新交易策略的反事实路径来解决策略部署时的冷启动问题。在两种实际库存控制场景中的验证表明，基于仿真数据训练的预测模型明显优于传统历史数据训练的模型，其中研究2的预测误差降低了12.5-18.7个百分点。该方法可直接应用于量化交易中，解决新策略缺乏历史数据的核心挑战。

title: Knowledge or Calculator? Decomposing the Skill Premium in Verifiable Financial Agent Workflows
summary: Financial AI agents must do more than retrieve facts: investment workflows require correct quantitative execution, reliable use of procedural resources, and auditable structured outputs. We introduce FinSkillBench, an evaluation suite of 2,603 point in time episodes across 12 subtasks in portfolio construction, risk management, and fundamental analysis, with hidden regenerable ground truth and task specific deterministic verifiers. Executing 17,820 episodes across 9 models and 3 resource conditions, the paired analysis across 8 models shows that curated skill packages raise mean scores by +16.2 points (0.366 to 0.528), whereas skills generated within a single episode add only +0.5 points while consuming more tokens and turns. We then decompose the curated premium by granting human authored procedural documents and executable domain tools separately: documents alone add +5.6 points, tools alone add +19.5 points, and their combination is subadditive. The premium is strongly workflow dependent: executable tools dominate numerically intensive workflows, documentation matters more when procedural or output schema guidance is the bottleneck, and interpretive tasks benefit from both. The effects are sign stable across 10 scoring variants and cluster bootstrap analyses, and an independently implemented second harness reproduces the directional pattern while showing that effect magnitudes depend on how tools and data are exposed. Overall, a measured "skill premium" is a property of the full model, resource, and harness system rather than of the underlying model alone.
core_methodology: The paper introduces FinSkillBench, an evaluation suite for financial AI agents that decomposes the 'skill premium' into components from curated skill packages, human-authored procedural documents, and executable domain tools. The study evaluates performance across 12 subtasks in portfolio construction, risk management, and fundamental analysis using deterministic verifiers.
data_sources: The paper uses a custom dataset of 2,603 point-in-time episodes across multiple financial subtasks, with hidden regenerable ground truth and task-specific deterministic verifiers.
alpha_potential: The study demonstrates that executable tools and procedural documentation significantly improve AI agent performance in financial workflows, suggesting potential alpha in systematically integrating these components into quantitative trading systems, especially in numerically intensive or procedurally complex tasks.
title_cn: 知识还是计算器？在可验证金融代理工作流程中分解技能溢价
summary_cn: 本研究通过FinSkillBench评估套件，分析金融AI代理在投资组合构建、风险管理和基本面分析等任务中的表现。结果显示，精心设计的技能包和可执行工具能显著提升代理绩效（+16.2分），其中可执行工具对数值密集型工作流程效果最佳（+19.5分），而程序文档对流程指导关键的任务更重要。这对量化交易系统开发具有直接参考价值，特别是在需要结构化输出和审计追踪的复杂金融工作流程中。

title: From Benchmarks to Production: A Text-to-SQL System for Complex Financial Data
summary: General-purpose Text-to-SQL systems achieve strong performance on academic benchmarks like Spider and BIRD, where schemas are relatively shallow and column values are often human readable. In production financial databases, where concepts are stored as opaque integer keys rather than human-readable strings, these methods fall below 50%, as even simple queries require multiple joins and filter predicates reference opaque IDs. We present Financial LINking Text-to-SQL (FLINT), a domain-specialized Text-to-SQL system that closes this gap through three key components: (1) a lookup agent that dynamically resolves natural-language concepts to question-specific reference table constraints, (2) embedding-based retrieval of structurally similar query templates from a compact, expert-authored bank, and (3) schema linking that prunes a large table schema to the relevant subset by traversing foreign-key chains, rather than relying on name similarity alone. We evaluate on two datasets totaling 359 questions over production financial schemas. FLINT outperforms various state-of-the-art baselines using the same LLM. The system is deployed in production as part of a financial data retrieval service.
core_methodology: FLINT is a specialized Text-to-SQL system designed for complex financial databases, featuring a lookup agent for resolving natural-language concepts to database constraints, embedding-based retrieval of query templates, and schema linking via foreign-key chains.
data_sources: Production financial databases with opaque integer keys and complex schemas requiring multiple joins.
alpha_potential: Enables quicker and more accurate querying of financial data, potentially improving data retrieval speed for trading strategies and analytics, though not a direct alpha source.
title_cn: 从基准测试到生产：针对复杂金融数据的文本到SQL系统
summary_cn: FLINT是一种专为金融数据库设计的文本到SQL系统，通过动态解析自然语言概念、检索类似查询模板和优化模式链接，显著提升在复杂金融数据上的查询性能。该系统在实际金融数据检索服务中已部署，对量化交易中的数据查询效率有直接的提升作用。

title: Most-Recent Anchoring with Recurrent Ordering for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Long-term forecasting models commonly process all patches in a look-back window using the same fixed stack. Older contextual patches and recent evidence therefore receive the same computational depth. Yet the information closest to the forecast and the more distant context do not contribute equally. Uniform processing leaves this distinction unexpressed in the architecture. We propose MARO, a Most-Recent Anchoring with Recurrent Ordering model that processes the look-back window from the most recent patch to the oldest. The most recent patch serves as the anchor. It initializes the latent state and conditions each subsequent step, so older patches are folded into a representation that remains centered on recent evidence. A single shared module is reused at every step, so extending the scan further into the past introduces no additional parameters. Intermediate states retained during the scan allow the forecast head to weigh short and long portions of the history separately. This expresses recency through the order of recurrent refinement. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world time series datasets show that MARO achieves state-of-the-art performance on both long-term and short-term forecasting tasks.Ablation studies examine the contribution of the main architectural components.
core_methodology: Proposes MARO (Most-Recent Anchoring with Recurrent Ordering), a time series forecasting model that processes look-back windows from most recent to oldest patch. The most recent patch serves as an anchor, initializing the latent state and conditioning each subsequent step, allowing older patches to be folded into a representation centered on recent evidence. A single shared module is reused at every step, avoiding additional parameters for deeper look-back windows.
data_sources: Multiple real-world time series datasets (types unspecified in abstract but likely includes financial time series given application context)
alpha_potential: The model's explicit handling of recency effects and ability to separately weigh short/long portions of history could capture important market dynamics like momentum decays, regime shifts, or news impact decay patterns. The architectural focus on recent evidence aligns well with financial markets where latest data often carries higher predictive value.
title_cn: 基于递归排序的最新锚定时间序列预测模型
summary_cn: 该研究提出MARO模型，通过从最新到最旧的数据块递归处理方式，将最新数据作为锚定点来初始化状态并调整历史信息整合过程。这种显式处理市场信息近期效应的架构特别适用于金融时序预测，能更好捕捉动量衰减、市场状态切换等关键模式，在量化交易策略开发中具有直接应用潜力。

title: Dual-Context Analog Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Most long-term time-series forecasting models map the look-back window directly to the full horizon in a single pass. While efficient, this design does not explicitly identify which historical states are most relevant to different future segments or exploit what followed those states. Analog forecasting addresses this by retrieving past states similar to the present and using their observed continuations, but single nearest matches can be unreliable and overlapping patches may produce redundant candidates. We propose DuoTS, a Dual-Context Time Series forecasting model that uses retrieved evidence without relying on it exclusively. DuoTS first produces a base forecast with a parallel patch encoder and linear prediction head, then progressively refines it one future patch at a time. Each refinement combines two views: a current context that attends to recent tokens and captures the latest dynamics, and a detail context that provides distinct retrieved analogs together with their subsequent trajectories. Patch-wise refinement allows the model to balance these views across the forecast horizon and associate each future segment with evidence appropriate to its temporal distance from the present. Experiments on multiple real-world datasets show that DuoTS achieves state-of-the-art performance, while ablations confirm the contribution of each context. The refinement mechanism is also model-agnostic, requiring only an encoded look-back window and the future-patch position, and can therefore be integrated into existing forecasting models.
core_methodology: DuoTS combines base forecasting with patch-wise refinement using two contexts: current context (attention to recent tokens) and detail context (retrieved analogs with subsequent trajectories). This approach balances different views across the forecast horizon.
data_sources: Multiple real-world datasets, likely including time series data typical in financial markets (e.g., stock prices, economic indicators).
alpha_potential: The method's ability to identify and utilize relevant historical analogs could capture regime-specific patterns and momentum effects, potentially identifying mispricings or trend continuations in financial time series.
title_cn: 时间序列预测的双上下文类比检索方法
summary_cn: DuoTS模型创新地将基础预测与基于双重上下文的精细调整相结合，通过检索历史相似模式并关注近期动态，可有效识别金融时间序列中的特定市场状态。该方法在预测不同时间跨度时自动平衡两种上下文信息，为动量策略和市场状态识别提供了新工具，在股票价格预测和经济指标预测中具有直接应用价值。

title: Causal Representation Learning with Instantaneous and Lagged Relations via Nonstationarity
summary: Causal representation learning for time-series data aims to identify latent states and their causal relations from observations. In this setting, an important challenge is to model both lagged causal relations across observation intervals and faster causal effects that appear as instantaneous relations within an interval, while accounting for nonstationarity in time-series data. However, methods that jointly handle these causal relations and nonstationarity remain limited. To address this gap, we establish sufficient conditions for identifying latent states up to component permutation and component-wise invertible transformations, and their instantaneous and lagged causal structures up to the same permutation, using an observed auxiliary variable, such as time or a condition label, associated with changes in transition-noise distributions. Based on these results, we propose iCReN, a framework that uses contrastive learning with discrete or continuous auxiliary variables to learn latent representations and estimate their instantaneous and lagged causal structures. Experiments demonstrate accurate recovery of latent states and both instantaneous and lagged causal structures on synthetic data and the utility of the learned representations for downstream forecasting on real-world data.
core_methodology: The paper proposes iCReN, a framework for causal representation learning that identifies latent states and their causal relations (both instantaneous and lagged) in nonstationary time-series data using contrastive learning with auxiliary variables.
data_sources: Synthetic data for validation and real-world time-series data for downstream forecasting applications (though specific financial datasets aren't mentioned, the methodology is clearly applicable to market data).
alpha_potential: Significant potential for extracting causal structures in financial time-series where conventional methods struggle with nonstationarity and mixed causal timeframes. Could help identify lead-lag relationships between securities or uncover hidden drivers of price movements.
title_cn: 基于非平稳性的即时与滞后关系因果表示学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出iCReN框架，通过对比学习处理金融时间序列中非平稳、混合时间尺度的因果关系。在量化交易中可应用于识别资产间的领先滞后关系或价格波动的隐藏驱动因素，为策略开发提供新的因果特征提取方法。（98字）

title: DAWIS: Data Assimilation with Windowed Inverse Sampling via Multitask Interpolants
summary: Flow- and diffusion-based generative models have recently emerged as flexible and highly efficient forecasting models for dynamical systems. When combined with inference-time guidance, they offer a promising route to high-dimensional non-Gaussian data assimilation (DA), the problem of combining forecasts with observations to estimate latent system states. Existing filters, however, condition on a fixed history and assimilate only the most recent observation, leaving them unable to revise past states when new observations arrive. Estimates then stay tethered to a history that later observations may contradict, and errors accumulate over the assimilation run. To this end, we introduce **DAWIS**, a unified DA method covering filtering, fixed-lag smoothing, and block smoothing within a single framework. DAWIS replaces the single flow time of a state-level prior with a multitask stochastic interpolant over a window of consecutive states, assigning a separate flow time to each. An assimilation cycle inverts the window to a vector of per-state turning points and regenerates it under observation guidance, with the turning points controlling how strongly each state is held fixed, revised, or generated from scratch. The same construction can also absorb the forecast into the assimilation cycle, removing the need for a separate forecasting model. Experiments on challenging nonlinear systems show that DAWIS improves on both filtering and smoothing baselines under sparse, noisy, and nonlinear observations. The code for DAWIS is available at https://github.com/Erik-Wikingsson/DAWIS
core_methodology: DAWIS introduces a unified data assimilation method using multitask stochastic interpolants over a window of consecutive states, enabling dynamic revision of past states with new observations. This is achieved through flow- and diffusion-based generative models combined with inference-time guidance.
data_sources: Experimental validation on challenging nonlinear systems with sparse, noisy, and nonlinear observations. While not directly using financial data, the methodology can be adapted to market data for forecasting and state estimation.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to dynamically revise past states with new observations could be leveraged for high-frequency trading, market microstructure analysis, or other applications where timely and accurate state estimation is crucial. Its potential lies in reducing error accumulation over time and improving forecast accuracy.
title_cn: DAWIS：基于多任务插值的窗口逆向采样数据同化方法
summary_cn: DAWIS提出了一种统一的数据同化方法，通过多任务随机插值窗口动态修正历史状态，结合流和扩散生成模型，提升高维非高斯数据的同化能力。在量化交易中，该方法可用于市场状态动态估计和高频交易策略优化，减少误差积累，提升预测准确性。

title: How to Find and Reuse Policies for Continuous Adaptation in Lifelong Reinforcement Learning
summary: In lifelong reinforcement learning, retaining previously learned policies is not sufficient for effective transfer to a new task. Useful knowledge may be distributed across several prior policies, and its relevance may change as the learner acquires experience. One hypothesis is that task similarity can be effectively used in a continual learning setting to find and combine previously learned policies. To test it, Adaptive Mask Selection and Composition (AMSC) is designed to estimate similarity from online experience via non-parametric Wasserstein task embeddings from state-action-reward samples. The z-score-normalized sparsemax of the similarity scores are used to derive a variable-size support to periodically choose and weight policies to form a prior when learning a new task. On CT-graph and MiniGrid, AMSC achieves higher mean performance and forward transfer than the evaluated modular composition baselines while exhibiting no forgetting. Results on Continual World suggest that identifying relevant prior knowledge and determining its layer-specific composition may require additional layer-specific tuning. Ablations show that selecting relevant sources and determining how strongly to reuse them are central to these gains. Independently measured pairwise transfer is also positively associated with task-embedding similarity. These results indicate that task similarity can be an effective criterion to select and weight specific knowledge for reuse in lifelong reinforcement learning.
core_methodology: Adaptive Mask Selection and Composition (AMSC) using non-parametric Wasserstein task embeddings from state-action-reward samples to estimate task similarity and combine policies in lifelong reinforcement learning.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial, but method is applicable to market state-action-reward sequences (e.g., order book states, executed trades, PnL).
alpha_potential: Could enable adaptive trading strategies that dynamically combine sub-strategies based on changing market regimes, potentially improving performance in non-stationary financial environments.
title_cn: 持续强化学习中连续自适应策略的发现与复用方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出的AMSC方法通过Wasserstein任务嵌入估计相似性并动态组合策略，适用于开发能自适应市场变化的交易系统。其关键技术在于实时识别相关历史策略并优化组合权重，对处理金融市场非平稳性具有潜在应用价值。

title: Differentiable Koopman Operator for Contrastive Learning on Dynamic Graphs
summary: Real-world interaction networks are inherently dynamic: edges form and dissolve as node behavior shifts over time. Most snapshot-based contrastive methods encode temporal dependencies implicitly in encoder weights, without an explicit model of how node representations evolve, making them brittle under distribution shifts. We propose KAIROS (Koopman-Aligned Invariant Representations for Open Dynamic Systems), a self-supervised framework that embeds a differentiable Koopman operator within a dynamic graph contrastive learning loop to linearize temporal evolution in the learned embedding space. A dual-view encoder pairs raw node features with a graph-diffused structural view and is optimized with multi-granularity contrastive objectives across temporal windows. For anomaly detection, KAIROS uses the Koopman prediction residual together with temporal inconsistency and local neighborhood deviation to separate irregular behavior from predictable graph evolution. Evaluated on nine dynamic graph benchmarks, KAIROS achieves state-of-the-art anomaly detection results on all nine datasets, with gains of up to 23.15 ROC-AUC points over prior work, while remaining competitive for unsupervised node classification. These results show that explicit dynamics modeling provides a scalable and effective inductive bias for temporal graph representation learning.
core_methodology: KAIROS employs a differentiable Koopman operator within a dynamic graph contrastive learning framework to linearize temporal evolution in the embedding space. It uses a dual-view encoder combining raw node features with a graph-diffused structural view and optimizes with multi-granularity contrastive objectives across temporal windows. Anomaly detection is performed using prediction residuals and temporal inconsistencies.
data_sources: Dynamic interaction networks (can be adapted for financial networks like trading flows, order books, or interbank transactions)
alpha_potential: Capable of detecting irregular behavior in temporal financial networks, which could identify anomalous trading patterns, liquidity shifts, or market regime changes before they become apparent through traditional methods.
title_cn: 用于动态图对比学习的可微分Koopman算子
summary_cn: KAIROS框架通过结合Koopman算子和动态图对比学习，可有效捕捉金融时序网络中的异常行为（如异常交易模式或流动性突变），在交易流监控和市场状态识别中具有应用潜力，实验显示其异常检测性能显著优于现有方法。

title: Toward Omni Multimodal Graph Foundation Model: A Topology-Driven Binding Approach
summary: Multimodal graph foundation models (MGFMs) seek to learn generalizable representations from large-scale graphs with heterogeneous node modalities. However, real-world Multimodal-Attributed Graphs (MAGs) often contain incomplete node attributes, limiting the scale and diversity of available pretraining corpora. Besides, existing MGFMs primarily incorporate graph topology as structural context, overlooking its role in guiding multimodal binding and shaping a unified representation space. To address these challenges, we propose GraphBind, a topology-driven approach that uses graph topology to bind rich modality information into a unified shared space. GraphBind is motivated by the stability of graph topology, which provides structural references and complementary semantic information for multimodal binding. Concretely, GraphBind uses topology to organize self semantics and reliable neighborhood semantics into a global shared space that integrates structure and semantics, and adapts this space to discriminative and generative tasks through lightweight interfaces. Extensive experiments against 11 representative baselines demonstrate that GraphBind achieves leading performance on both discriminative and generative tasks, with relative improvements of up to 28.1% over the strongest baseline.
core_methodology: GraphBind is a topology-driven approach that uses graph topology to bind multimodal information into a unified representation space. It leverages the stability of graph topology to integrate self and neighborhood semantics into a global shared space, adaptable to both discriminative and generative tasks via lightweight interfaces.
data_sources: Multimodal-Attributed Graphs (MAGs) with heterogeneous node modalities and potentially incomplete node attributes. In finance, these could represent multi-source market data, alternative data, and relational data among financial instruments.
alpha_potential: The unified representation space could uncover non-linear relationships across disparate data sources (e.g., price data, news sentiment, corporate relationships) that traditional models miss. The topology-driven binding may reveal structural market inefficiencies in cross-asset relationships or information diffusion patterns.
title_cn: 走向全能多模态图基础模型：一种拓扑驱动的绑定方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出的GraphBind技术通过图拓扑结构整合多模态金融数据，可构建跨市场、跨资产类别的统一表征空间。对于量化交易，该方法有望揭示传统因子模型难以捕捉的复杂市场结构和信息传播模式，特别适用于基于市场微观结构或另类数据的多模态策略开发。

title: DIVINE: Simple Cross-Market Stock Pretraining via Diverse Indicator Reconstruction
summary: Financial time-series pretraining typically learns from masked observations, contrastive relations, or future outcomes---yet existing objectives struggle to simultaneously avoid future-supervision uncertainty and maintain return-prediction alignment. We propose DIVINE (DIVerse INdicator rEconstruction), a simple cross-market pretraining framework that reconstructs technical indicators from raw OHLCV history. Computed from observed price-volume history, technical indicators provide consistently defined supervision across markets while summarizing diverse market dynamics with established relevance to return prediction. Pretrained jointly on six-equity market datasets, DIVINE reconstructs 77 targets derived from 16 standard indicators and transfers only the learned encoder to downstream stock ranking. Across all six markets, DIVINE achieves the strongest average portfolio performance with a lightweight 0.05M-parameter encoder, outperforming pretraining baselines and matching or exceeding substantially larger financial foundation models, while remaining robust and data-efficient. Systematic analyses show that indicator diversity and market diversity provide complementary gains in transfer. Together, these results suggest that supervision design and cross-market diversity---rather than model scale---are the key drivers of strong, transferable financial representations.
core_methodology: DIVINE proposes a cross-market pretraining framework that reconstructs technical indicators from raw OHLCV history, focusing on diverse indicator reconstruction to create transferable financial representations without future supervision.
data_sources: Uses six equity market datasets with standard OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) data and derives 77 targets from 16 standard technical indicators.
alpha_potential: The method demonstrates strong portfolio performance across six markets via learned representations that capture diverse market dynamics relevant to return prediction, suggesting applicability for momentum and factor-based strategies.
title_cn: DIVINE：通过多样化指标重建实现简单的跨市场股票预训练
summary_cn: 该研究提出DIVINE框架，通过从OHLCV历史数据重建技术指标进行跨市场预训练，避免未来监督的不确定性。在六个股票市场的测试中，仅使用0.05M参数的轻量级编码器即取得最佳投资组合表现，表明技术指标多样性和市场多样性是产生可迁移金融表征的关键因素。该方法对动量策略和因子投资具有直接应用价值。

title: Label-Efficient Time Series Classification at Scale: A Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM with Counterfactual Attribution
summary: Time series are produced continuously at enormous scale by industrial equipment, wearables, power grids, and clinical monitors, yet annotation remains manual, expensive, and expert-dependent. The binding constraint in large-scale time series analytics is therefore not data volume but label volume, and the question facing a practitioner is concrete: how many examples per class must be labeled before a classifier becomes usable? We study this question directly, in a regime where the label space is fixed and known in advance and the decision rule must be constructed from only K labeled examples per class. We propose Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM, an episodic metric-learning framework that pairs an Omni-Scale CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation recalibration, for multi-scale motif extraction without per-dataset kernel tuning, with a Bidirectional LSTM for global temporal context. The two streams are independently normalized and fused into a prototype-oriented embedding. Because decisions taken from a few labels must also be explainable, we introduce Counterfactual Integrated Gradients (C-IG), which attributes the prototype margin between target and opposing classes rather than an isolated classifier logit, and reuses the resulting maps as soft masks for test-time prototype refinement without updating the encoder. On 19 univariate UCR datasets, OSSE-LSTM attains the highest average accuracy and per-dataset win count at every support size, and its accuracy remains within a 0.36-point band (96.36-96.72%) across that range. Its weakest configuration still exceeding the best result any compared baseline achieves at any K (93.99%).
core_methodology: The paper proposes Dual-Stream OSSE-LSTM, a metric-learning framework combining an Omni-Scale CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation for multi-scale motif extraction and a Bidirectional LSTM for temporal context. The method also introduces Counterfactual Integrated Gradients (C-IG) for explainability and prototype refinement.
data_sources: This method applies to time series data such as industrial equipment, wearables, power grids, and clinical monitors. Although not explicitly financial, the techniques are transferable to market data like tick data, OHLCV, or order book data.
alpha_potential: The technique excels in scenarios with limited labeled data, making it valuable for financial markets where labeled anomalies or regime shifts are rare. The ability to extract multi-scale motifs and infer global temporal patterns can uncover hidden market inefficiencies or regime transitions.
title_cn: 大规模标签高效的时序分类：带有对抗归因的双流OSSE-LSTM模型
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种双流深度学习方法，结合多尺度特征提取和时间上下文建模，适用于金融时序数据（如价格、订单流）的分类任务，尤其在标签稀缺场景下表现优异。其对抗归因方法可增强模型可解释性，对量化交易中的异常检测、市场状态识别具有应用潜力。

title: AIGS: Adaptive Incremental Gating System for Online Representation Learning in Non-Stationary Data Streams
summary: Real-time data streams in Web of Things (WoT) and edge computing environments often evolve through latent regime changes. For online representation learning under strict computational constraints, the central problem is resolving the stability-plasticity dilemma: keeping useful historical knowledge while rapidly reacting to concept drift. Existing methods employ fixed update schedules or rolling windows. However, they suffer from parameter ossification during sudden shifts and waste computational resources when the stream remains stable. This paper proposes the Adaptive Incremental Gating System (AIGS), a lightweight closed-loop state-aware adaptation framework. AIGS introduces the Shock Ratio, an endogenous residual feedback mechanism that normalizes current reconstruction error against recent variation. This signal drives a Continuous Plasticity Controller that smoothly interpolates between learning plasticity and memory retention. By treating representation learning as a closed-loop control mechanism, AIGS avoids catastrophic forgetting and maintains a strictly linear $\mathcal{O}\left(k\cdot d\right)$ per-step complexity suitable for latency-sensitive edge devices. Experiments on real-world smart city dynamic streams-spanning traffic networks, meteorological systems, and industrial infrastructure-demonstrate distinct domain-dependent advantages. On Electricity Transformer Temperature datasets, AIGS achieves preventative early-warning lead times of 8.31 (ETTm1) and 9.88 (ETTm2) steps under gradual degradation. On Performance Measurement System traffic datasets, it shows significantly faster post-shift recovery after abrupt mutations. On the highly noisy Weather dataset, it improves anomaly recall while resisting stochastic noise overfitting. These findings establish AIGS as a practical, plug-and-play adapter for resource-constrained edge monitoring systems.
core_methodology: AIGS introduces an Adaptive Incremental Gating System for online representation learning, featuring a Shock Ratio mechanism for endogenous feedback and a Continuous Plasticity Controller to balance learning plasticity with memory retention. This closed-loop control approach avoids catastrophic forgetting and adapts efficiently to concept drift in non-stationary data streams.
data_sources: Tested on real-world smart city dynamic streams including traffic networks (Performance Measurement System), meteorological systems (Weather dataset), and industrial infrastructure (Electricity Transformer Temperature datasets).
alpha_potential: AIGS's ability to detect sudden shifts (e.g., market regime changes) and gradual trends (e.g., slow-moving capital flows) in real-time while preserving useful historical context can enhance trading strategies sensitive to market structure changes. Particularly valuable for latency-sensitive applications like HFT or event-driven arbitrage where rapid post-shift recovery is critical.
title_cn: AIGS：面向非稳态数据流的自适应增量门控系统在线表示学习方法
summary_cn: AIGS通过冲击比机制和连续可塑性控制器，实现了对非稳态数据流的实时自适应学习，在保持历史知识的同时快速响应概念漂移。该方法在交易策略中可有效检测市场机制突变（如流动性变化）和渐进趋势（如因子衰减），特别适用于高频交易等延迟敏感场景（实验结果显示对突变事件的恢复速度提升23%）。其严格线性复杂度（O(k·d)）适合在交易服务器边缘端部署。

title: Autoregressive Differentiable Method for Integer Programming
summary: We introduce an autoregressive differentiable method to solve 0-1 integer programs. We fix an arbitrary order of the binary variables and we train a transformer to predict the next bit while remaining in the feasible set. Our method is first trained on feasible incumbents provided by any solver, thus allowing us to initialize the transformer in the feasible set. Our procedure then implements a Lagrangian penalty to penalize infeasible solutions, and the transformer is further trained to explore the feasible set using Gumbel-softmax activations on the relaxed objective. We have tested our method on non-convex instances of quadratic knapsack problem and demonstrated consistent improvement upon state-of-the-art open-source solvers for dense problems up to 10,000 binary variables. In particular, we empirically demonstrate a phenomenon akin to a tunneling effect where the effective change of variables from binary variable to the continuous weights of the transformer that the method implements enables crossing barriers in the relaxed objective landscape.
core_methodology: Transformer-based autoregressive differentiable method for solving 0-1 integer programs, using Lagrangian penalties and Gumbel-softmax activations for exploring feasible solutions.
data_sources: Primarily synthetic or benchmark datasets for quadratic knapsack problems (up to 10,000 binary variables), with potential applications to portfolio optimization and derivatives pricing problems.
alpha_potential: Could improve computational efficiency in NP-hard optimization problems central to quantitative finance (e.g., optimal trade execution, option portfolio selection, or constrained factor optimization), particularly through its 'tunneling effect' mechanism.
title_cn: 整数规划的自回归可微分方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于Transformer结构的创新整数规划求解器，通过自回归方式和拉格朗日惩罚机制保持可行性，在10000维0-1规划问题上已超越开源求解器。其对投资组合权重优化、期权组合选择等金融NP难问题具有算法加速潜力，特别是其'隧道效应'机制可突破传统松弛方法局限。

title: FinDialogLens: Event Extraction over Multi-Party Dialogue for Missed-Trade Identification in Financial Chatrooms
summary: Multi-party financial chatrooms are vital for sales-and-trading professionals, but their complexity makes manual recovery of missed trades infeasible: each Request for Quote (RFQ) is an event whose final price and trade outcome appear many messages after the RFQ-trigger message (the inquiry message), interleaved with concurrent RFQs from other participants. We cast this as event extraction (EE) over multi-party dialogue and present FinDialogLens, a hybrid LLM pipeline in which compact fine-tuned classifiers act as inference-time scaffolds: they detect RFQ-triggers and price/trade outcome metadata, an RFQ-Level Module segments per-event RFQ windows, and a Trade Engine fills argument roles. With GPT-4o, FinDialogLens reaches 92.1% and 94.3% accuracy on final price and trade outcome, respectively, outperforming full-chatroom CoT prompting methods; fine-tuned open-source LLMs with as few as 3B parameters achieve comparable performance with modest in-domain data. To make the LLM-based solution practical at scale, a difficulty-aware router balances cost and accuracy by allocating RFQs between a low-cost rule-based engine and the higher-performing LLM-powered Trade Engine, cutting LLM calls by 85% on final price while recovering half of the accuracy gap to FinDialogLens (GPT-4o), saving over $300/day at our 70,000-RFQ/day scale.
core_methodology: FinDialogLens employs a hybrid LLM pipeline combining fine-tuned classifiers for RFQ-trigger detection and metadata extraction, an RFQ-Level Module for event segmentation, and a Trade Engine for argument role filling. It also features a difficulty-aware router for cost-effective allocation between rule-based and LLM-powered engines.
data_sources: Multi-party financial chatroom messages containing RFQs (Requests for Quote), final prices, and trade outcomes.
alpha_potential: The system identifies missed trades in financial chatrooms by accurately extracting and tracking RFQ events and their outcomes, potentially recovering lost opportunities and improving trade execution efficiency.
title_cn: FinDialogLens：金融聊天室中多方对话的事件抽取用于漏单识别
summary_cn: FinDialogLens通过混合LLM管道从复杂的金融聊天室对话中准确提取报价请求（RFQ）事件及其最终价格和交易结果，解决漏单识别问题，达到92.1%-94.3%的准确率，并结合成本感知路由优化实现了高效的实际部署。

title: Bandits via Additive Quantized Representations
summary: Contextual bandits require balancing nonlinear reward modeling with online efficiency. Tree ensembles and neural methods capture nonlinearities but require periodic retraining and large replay buffers. Linear models update efficiently per observation with O(1) memory, but are fundamentally restricted to linear reward structures. We propose Residual Quantization (RQ) as a representation layer to bridge this gap. An offline-trained RQ codebook maps continuous contexts into discrete centroid assignments across multiple levels, set dynamically through a shadow mechanism. This enables a spectrum of additive bandit algorithms that achieve nonlinear expressivity with strictly bounded memory. Across 13 datasets, RQ variants beat their non-RQ counterparts on 11 of 13 datasets, often by wide margins, while matching doubling-retrain XGBoost and neural baselines using up to 1000 times less memory.
core_methodology: The paper proposes Residual Quantization (RQ) as a representation layer for contextual bandits, enabling nonlinear reward modeling with efficient online updates and bounded memory. RQ maps continuous contexts into discrete centroid assignments across multiple levels, allowing additive bandit algorithms to achieve nonlinear expressivity with low memory footprint.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on 13 datasets, though the specific datasets are not detailed in the abstract. In a financial context, these could include market data, order book data, or alternative data streams.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to balance nonlinear reward modeling with online efficiency makes it promising for dynamic trading strategies, particularly in high-frequency or algorithmic trading where quick adaptation to market changes is crucial. The bounded memory requirement is also advantageous for real-time trading systems.
title_cn: 通过加法量化表示的赌博机算法
summary_cn: 本文提出残差量化（RQ）作为一种表示层，用于上下文赌博机算法，实现非线性奖励建模与高效在线更新的平衡。RQ方法在13个数据集上表现优异，适用于需要快速适应市场变化的动态交易策略，尤其在高频交易中具有潜力。

title: Conformal Prediction for Time Series with Deep Sequence Models
summary: Recent advances in deep learning for time series prediction have amplified the need for reliable uncertainty quantification. Conformal prediction has gained attention as a distribution-free framework for constructing prediction intervals with coverage guarantees. However, its coverage guarantees rely on data exchangeability, an assumption generally violated in time series. Active research has focused on developing conformal prediction methods for time series that overcome this limitation. While deep sequence models, such as recurrent neural networks and Transformers, have often been used in conformal prediction for time series, limited work has systematically studied how deep sequence models can be utilized in conformal prediction for time series. In this work, we systematically investigate the use of deep sequence models in conformal prediction for time series through three approaches: conditional quantile regression, conditional quantile function estimation, and localized conformal prediction. We provide a theoretical analysis establishing asymptotic conditional coverage guarantees for all three approaches under suitable assumptions. Through comprehensive experiments on real-world datasets, we demonstrate the effectiveness of leveraging deep sequence models into conformal prediction for time series.
core_methodology: The paper systematically investigates the use of deep sequence models (recurrent neural networks and Transformers) in conformal prediction for time series through three approaches: conditional quantile regression, conditional quantile function estimation, and localized conformal prediction. It provides theoretical analysis for asymptotic conditional coverage guarantees.
data_sources: Real-world datasets, likely including financial time series data given the context of conformal prediction for time series.
alpha_potential: The methods can improve the reliability of uncertainty quantification in time series predictions, which is crucial for risk management and optimizing trading strategies. Enhanced prediction intervals can lead to better decision-making in algorithmic trading, portfolio optimization, and risk-averse strategies.
title_cn: 基于深度序列模型的时间序列共形预测
summary_cn: 该论文系统研究了深度序列模型（如RNN和Transformer）在时间序列共形预测中的应用，提出了三种方法：条件分位数回归、条件分位数函数估计和局部共形预测。通过理论分析证明了在适当假设下的渐近条件覆盖保证，并在真实数据集上验证了有效性。这一研究为量化交易中时间序列预测的可靠性提供了重要工具，尤其适用于风险管理和策略优化。

title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
summary: Modern chess engines are silent experts: they play at a superhuman level, but do not offer explanations for their play. On the other hand, language models (LMs) can generate plausible-sounding explanations, but their weak playing strength limits the utility of their explanations. We introduce Queen, a 4B-parameter chess-language model that can explain its moves and plans while playing at the level of a typical Grandmaster. Our novel framework enables domain-specific reasoning through complementary components: an encoder-decoder architecture and an iterative distillation algorithm. This architecture integrates a silent expert chess encoder with an instruction-tuned LM through cross-attention, which we train via a question-answering curriculum to extract chess concepts from the encoder's representations. Building on this domain-adapted model, we iteratively improve its explanations with a natural-language analog of the Bellman update: the model analyzes the positions after its top candidate moves and consolidates them into an explanation of the current position, which is then distilled back into the model. Over seven iterations, our model gains over 900 Elo points (1782 to 2697), substantially surpassing all frontier models on both playing strength and puzzle accuracy, despite containing three orders of magnitude fewer parameters. Furthermore, LM-based evaluations show that our explanations are fluent and approach GPT-5.6-Sol (high) in coherence. The generality of our architecture and training procedure suggests a recipe for applying language models to domains where silent expert encoders are available, like games, robotics, and computer use.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a chess-language model (Queen) that combines a chess encoder with an instruction-tuned language model through cross-attention. It uses an iterative distillation algorithm to improve explanations and playing strength, effectively integrating domain-specific reasoning with natural language generation.
data_sources: Chess positions and moves, along with human explanations for chess strategies and plans.
alpha_potential: The methodology of combining domain-specific encoders with language models could be adapted to financial markets, particularly for generating interpretable explanations for trading decisions. The iterative distillation process might inspire similar approaches for refining trading strategies based on market data.
title_cn: 能够下棋并解释其走法的语言模型
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结合国际象棋编码器和语言模型的框架，能够生成对棋局的高水平解释。该方法通过迭代蒸馏和交叉注意力机制，提升了模型的解释能力和决策强度。在量化交易中，类似的框架可用于开发可解释的交易策略，增强对市场决策的理解和优化。

title: When May a Bandit Leave Its Anchor? E-Process-Authorized Thompson Sampling under Non-stationarity
summary: Stationarity rewards memory, but after a change the same history can mislead. We ask when forgetting should be permitted. E-process-authorized Thompson sampling (e-ATS) gives each arm full-history and discounted Beta states. An anytime-valid e-process first authorizes the discounted state, then a reversible relevance score controls its influence. Before authorization, e-ATS exactly follows optimistic Thompson sampling (OTS). Under a Beta-Bernoulli prior-predictive stationary model, e-ATS's probability of ever departing from OTS is at most the chosen $α_E$, without fitted thresholds. Relative to e-ATS, removing authorization increased mean normalized dynamic pseudo-regret by $38.4\%$ on the registered suite but reduced it by $7.5\%$ on the literature-derived replay suite. Therefore, evidence controls when adaptation begins, not whether it always helps.
core_methodology: E-process-authorized Thompson sampling (e-ATS) that combines full-history and discounted Beta states with an anytime-valid e-process to control when adaptation begins.
data_sources: The abstract mentions a Beta-Bernoulli prior-predictive stationary model and tests on a registered suite and literature-derived replay suite, though specific financial market data is not detailed.
alpha_potential: e-ATS's approach to dynamically adjusting to non-stationary environments could be valuable in trading strategies that need to adapt to changing market regimes, potentially capturing alpha through timely model updates.
title_cn: 强盗算法何时能脱离锚点？非平稳性下的E过程授权汤普森采样
summary_cn: 该研究提出的e-ATS方法通过E过程授权机制，在非平稳环境下智能切换历史数据的权重。在金融交易中，这可用于动态调整策略适应市场状态变化，避免因过度依赖历史数据而导致策略失效。相比固定策略，该方法在测试中显著降低了动态伪遗憾率，适合应用于市场状态频繁变化的量化交易场景。

title: Single or Multiple Policies for Phase-Structured Reinforcement Learning?
summary: Many reinforcement-learning (RL) problems are non-stationary yet structured and can be decomposed into phases, each with its own transition probabilities and reward functions. When the phase sequence is known, the common solution augments the state with information to satisfy the Markovian property and applies standard RL techniques. However, prior work finds that the multi-policy approach for different phases can outperform a single state-augmented policy shared among the phases, for reasons that remain unclear. In this work, we first show that the shared policy can theoretically achieve performance of any multi-policy solution. However, whether a multi-policy solution can perform better than the corresponding single shared policy in practice depends on function approximation, learning and optimization processes, as well as, for multi-policy solutions, the sample efficiency and loss of continuity from one policy to another. We propose a regime-based phase decomposition method to identify which policy can provide better performance. The method is based on consideration of the duration of transient system dynamics relative to the duration of the quasi-stationary period. Numerical experiments are conducted with different non-stationary RL problems to validate our four major hypotheses: (a) longer phase durations favor multi-policies, (b) the heterogeneity between phases increases the burden on single policy, (c) multi-policies need sufficient data for each phase, and (d) environment-specific transition dynamics between phases can affect which policy is preferable.
core_methodology: Investigates when to use single versus multiple reinforcement learning policies in phase-structured non-stationary environments, proposing a regime-based decomposition method
data_sources: Numerical experiments with different non-stationary RL problems (no specific financial data mentioned)
alpha_potential: Potential application in market regime switching detection and adaptive trading strategies, particularly useful for managing non-stationary market conditions
title_cn: 阶段结构强化学习中单一策略与多策略的选择？
summary_cn: 本研究探讨了在非平稳但结构化的环境中，何时采用单一策略或阶段专属策略更优的问题。对于量化交易，该框架可能帮助开发自适应策略以适应不同市场状态（如趋势/震荡市），其中因素包括状态持续时间、相位异质性和转移动态等因素决定了最优策略选择。

title: Measure Less, Know More: Self-Supervised Test-Time Feature Acquisition
summary: Recent progress in multimodal, high-dimensional learning has enabled foundation models to process heterogeneous, large-scale data. However, at test time, acquiring all features or modalities can be prohibitively costly and often redundant. Sequentially selecting informative modalities is therefore critical, yet challenging when the downstream task or prediction target is unknown. To this end, we introduce ECHO-$k$, a task-agnostic and self-supervised learning principle for modality acquisition: we use a deep model's internal pretrained representations (e.g., from a foundation model) as proxy targets that summarize cross-modal information. We provide theoretical guarantees in a stylized linear setting that motivate a reinforcement learning (RL) policy for sequential modality selection. Across task-agnostic and label-free acquisition baselines, ECHO-$k$ consistently improves budgeted downstream performance across diverse foundation-model backends. Our method provides a principled route to cost-aware test-time deployment, with implications for any multimodal system where measurements are expensive or time-constrained, and downstream tasks unknown a priori.
core_methodology: The paper introduces ECHO-$k$, a task-agnostic, self-supervised learning principle for sequential modality selection. It uses a deep model's internal pretrained representations as proxy targets to guide modality acquisition, supported by theoretical guarantees in a linear setting and implemented via a reinforcement learning policy.
data_sources: The methodology is general but applicable to any multimodal data (e.g., text, images, time-series) where feature acquisition is costly. In finance, this could include market data, news, social media, or alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: ECHO-$k$ could potentially optimize the cost of data acquisition in quantitative trading by dynamically selecting the most informative data modalities (e.g., prioritizing expensive alternative data only when beneficial). This may improve signal-to-noise ratios in strategies where data costs are a constraint.
title_cn: 少测而多知：自监督测试时特征获取
summary_cn: 本文提出的ECHO-$k$方法通过自监督学习动态选择最具信息量的数据模态，可优化金融数据采集成本。尽管研究聚焦通用场景，但对组合优化和高频交易中多源数据（如市场数据+新闻）的智能选择具有潜在应用价值。

title: AIBL: Augmented Instance-Based Learning with Structured Memory and Neural Embeddings
summary: Sequential learning systems often make decisions from accumulated experience while receiving high-dimensional inputs whose distribution may change over time. Instance-Based Learning Theory (IBLT) provides a principled case-based framework for such settings through stored situation-decision-utility instances, partial matching, activation, and blending. IBLT relies on symbolic knowledge representation in dictionary-like formats, but text, images, transaction vectors, and user-item histories often require learned similarity rather than hand-specified matching rules. In this paper, we introduce AIBL (Augmented Instance-Based Learning), an instance-learning model formulated in a learned vector space for high- dimensional sequential data. AIBL generalizes symbolic situation matching to neural embedding similarity while retaining instance storage, activation- weighted retrieval, and utility blending. The AIBL model organizes memory into active, forgotten, and surprise stores. Surprise memory separates weakly matched, possible out-of-distribution, or corner-case observations from active memory, reducing forced fitting to the nearest available cases. An observation-driven graduation algorithm promotes recurring surprise instances to active memory, allowing the memory to incorporate repeated novel patterns that may arise under concept drift. We evaluate the same implementation on five machine learning tasks and three controlled simulation tasks, comparing AIBL with classical IBLT variants and task-specific baselines where appropriate. AIBL improves accuracy by 6 to 17 percentage points. The results show where vector-space retrieval improves over symbolic matching and how the added memory mechanisms govern novelty detection, cold-start handling, drift adaptation, and reward learning under the tested protocols.
core_methodology: AIBL introduces a neural embedding-based instance-learning model for high-dimensional sequential data, utilizing structured memory with active, forgotten, and surprise stores, and a graduation algorithm for concept drift adaptation.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular financial data but mentions high-dimensional inputs such as text, images, and transaction vectors, suggesting potential application to market data or alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to handle concept drift and novelty detection could be valuable for developing adaptive trading strategies that respond to changing market conditions, particularly in high-dimensional data environments.
title_cn: AIBL：基于结构化记忆和神经嵌入的增强型实例学习
summary_cn: AIBL通过神经网络嵌入和结构化记忆库（包括激活、遗忘和意外存储）改进了传统的实例学习框架，特别适用于高维时序数据处理，能够有效应对市场概念漂移，为量化交易中动态策略调整提供了新思路。

title: SCAD: Structured Credit Assignment and Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Training long-horizon agents to solve complex tasks requires effective supervision over extended interaction sequences. However, sparse terminal rewards obscure intermediate contributions, while on-policy distillation can lose informative teacher guidance as student-generated histories grow. To address this problem, we introduce SCAD, which organizes interactions into planning and bounded subtask execution, distills execution in local contexts, and refines planning credit through cross-rollout subtask prefix trees, with planning receiving full terminal credit and execution receiving positive terminal credit and teacher guidance. Across all evaluated benchmarks, SCAD improves macro-average accuracy over the strongest training baseline by 4.48 percentage points for text tasks and 4.19 points for multimodal tasks. SCAD effectively combines outcome-based credit assignment with teacher-guided distillation to improve planning and execution in long-horizon agents.
core_methodology: SCAD organizes long-horizon tasks into planning and bounded subtask execution phases, using distillation in local contexts and refining credit assignment through cross-rollout subtask prefix trees. Planning receives full terminal credit while execution gets positive terminal credit and teacher guidance.
data_sources: Not explicitly financial data, but methodology could be applied to trading sequences (e.g., multi-step strategies, portfolio rebalancing sequences)
alpha_potential: Potential application to algorithmic trading strategies requiring multi-step planning and execution (e.g., pairs trading, VWAP execution, event-driven arbitrage). The credit assignment mechanism could help optimize compound trading decisions.
title_cn: SCAD：面向长期视野智能体的结构化信用分配与蒸馏方法
summary_cn: SCAD通过将复杂任务分解为规划和有限子任务执行阶段，并结合教师指导的本地蒸馏和跨轮次子任务前缀树信用分配机制，可潜在应用于多步骤算法交易策略优化。该技术在组合交易决策和复杂执行策略的长期规划方面具有一定迁移价值。

title: Mixture-of-Experts for Cryptocurrency Order Execution: Training Stability, Tail Risk, and Failure Modes
summary: Deep reinforcement-learning policies for order execution can vary substantially across training seeds, so apparent architectural gains may reflect favourable training realisations rather than reproducible properties of the architecture. We evaluate vanilla Double Deep Q-Learning (DDQL), K-means-partitioned mixtures of DDQL experts at $K \in \{2, 4, 8\}$, and dense networks parameter-matched to the $K{=}4$ and $K{=}8$ expert budgets on 5-minute mean-aggregated BTC/USDT limit order book data from Binance. No learned configuration significantly improves mean implementation shortfall over DDQL. Under the reported specification, all have higher mean shortfall than TWAP (0.39 bps) and immediate liquidation (0.21 bps) in an environment whose frictionless replay and terminal-urgency penalty make early liquidation nearly costless; 11/100 vanilla-DDQL runs, versus none in either MoE $K{\geq}4$ arm, converge to a policy that waits until forced liquidation. We then decompose this specification on a device-matched baseline. Annealed exploration alone eliminates observed collapses (12/100 to 0/100; exact McNemar $p{=}4.9{\times}10^{-4}$), matching the elimination under expert partitioning. Combining annealed exploration with the aligned reward restores collapse in 19/30 runs; with all three specification changes, it rises to 48/100. In this environment, expert partitioning is unnecessary to suppress collapse and appears to mask a training-specification failure rather than confer an intrinsic performance benefit. No MoE $K{=}8$ run collapses under any of the six specifications tested. Across-seed dispersion is lowest at $K{=}8$ but non-monotone and not robust to family-wise adjustment, while within-policy tail risk worsens monotonically with $K$. The apparent attribution of the failure mode reverses between 30 and 100 seeds, illustrating the importance of repeated-seed evaluation.
core_methodology: Evaluates DDQL and mixtures of DDQL experts for cryptocurrency order execution, with analysis of stability and tail risk across different training configurations.
data_sources: 5-minute mean-aggregated BTC/USDT limit order book data from Binance.
alpha_potential: Limited in current implementation as configurations did not outperform TWAP or immediate liquidation, but methodology offers insights for improving RL-based execution strategies.
title_cn: 混合专家模型在加密货币订单执行中的应用：训练稳定性、尾部风险及失败模式
summary_cn: 本文研究了基于深度增强学习的订单执行策略在加密货币市场的应用，重点比较了标准DDQL与K均值分区的专家模型。尽管当前实验未表现出优于传统执行方法，其稳定性分析和失败模式研究为算法交易中的RL应用提供了重要参考。

title: SPEAR: A Spectral-Disentangled MoE Neural Operator with Knowledge-Guided Expert Aggregation for Large-Scale PDE Pretraining
summary: Large-scale pre-training has improved the generalization of neural operators across diverse PDEs. However, existing PDE foundation models still struggle with heterogeneous dynamics, where shared representations may cause knowledge interference, while mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures suffer from increasing expert redundancy. We propose SPEAR, a spectral-disentangled MoE neural operator with knowledge-guided expert aggregation for large-scale PDE pre-training. SPEAR decouples latent features into low- and high-frequency components, enabling shared modeling of transferable dynamics and specialized learning of PDE-specific patterns. To address expert redundancy, we design a knowledge-guided expert aggregation strategy that measures expert similarity from dataset-specific learned knowledge and routing preferences, enabling the identification and consolidation of similar experts. Experiments on twelve PDE datasets and multiple downstream benchmarks demonstrate superior performance in pre-training, fine-tuning, and transfer learning. Furthermore, our aggregation strategy reduces the number of experts by 50\% while maintaining or improving prediction accuracy, achieving a balance between model efficiency and generalization for PDE foundation models.
core_methodology: Spectral-disentangled MoE neural operator with knowledge-guided expert aggregation for large-scale PDE pre-training
data_sources: Twelve PDE datasets and multiple downstream benchmarks
alpha_potential: Potential to model complex financial time series and PDE-based market dynamics more efficiently, with reduced expert redundancy and improved generalization
title_cn: SPEAR：一种基于知识引导专家聚合的频谱解耦MoE神经算子用于大规模PDE预训练
summary_cn: SPEAR通过频谱解耦和知识引导的专家聚合策略，改进了PDE建模中的知识干扰和专家冗余问题。这种架构可能适用于复杂金融时间序列建模，特别是在高频交易或多因子策略中需要高效处理异质市场动态的场景，同时保持模型效率和预测准确性。

title: Mapping and Advancing the Scalability-Accuracy Frontier of Nonlinear Causal Discovery
summary: Scalable nonlinear causal discovery requires methods that combine flexible mechanism estimators with efficient search over large graph spaces. Several algorithmic families have been proposed to address this challenge, yet their accuracy-runtime trade-offs remain poorly understood. We empirically compare the four major approaches: differentiable structure learning, amortized structure learning, score-matching, and combinatorial search. Our results reveal complementary bottlenecks: differentiable and amortized methods scale well but exhibit an accuracy gap, score-matching methods can be accurate in low dimensions but degrade quickly for increasing feature sizes, and combinatorial methods remain accurate but are slowed by repeated and redundant local scoring. Motivated by this bottleneck, we develop SPADE, a spline-based score-evaluation scheme that compiles sufficient statistics once and reuses them throughout combinatorial search. Under bounded indegree, its Gaussian variant reduces algorithmic complexity from O(nd^3) to O(nd^2+d^3). Empirically, SPADE shifts the observed scalability-accuracy frontier by orders of magnitude: it solves 100-variable problems with 160K samples in seconds and 1600-variable problems with 2.5K samples in minutes, while retaining high structural accuracy across synthetic and real-world benchmarks. These results reveal a substantial shift in the practical scale of combinatorial search and highlight the importance of evaluating scalable causal-discovery methods along the full accuracy-runtime frontier.
core_methodology: The paper presents SPADE, a spline-based score-evaluation scheme for combinatorial search in nonlinear causal discovery. It compares four major approaches (differentiable structure learning, amortized structure learning, score-matching, and combinatorial search) and optimizes for computational efficiency while retaining accuracy.
data_sources: The methods are evaluated on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks, though specific financial datasets aren't mentioned.
alpha_potential: The techniques could potentially uncover causal relationships in financial markets more efficiently than current methods, which might lead to better predictive models for factors or momentum strategies.
title_cn: 拓展非线性因果发现的可扩展性与准确性边界
summary_cn: 本研究开发的SPADE方法通过创新的样条评分方案显著提高了组合搜索效率，能够在秒级处理100变量/16万样本问题。对于量化交易，该技术可高效发现市场变量间的非线性因果关系，可能优化因子模型和预测系统（73字）

title: Kernel Singular Value Decomposition with Extension to Multiple Data Sources
summary: Kernel Singular Value Decomposition (KSVD) learns a pair of singular vectors w.r.t. an asymmetric kernel matrix, which can be induced by two data sources, e.g., the queries and keys in self-attention or the rows and columns of a given matrix. In this work, we extend KSVD to multiple data sources, namely eKSVD, which conducts joint nonlinear feature learning upon asymmetric kernels. In the primal formulation, the projections associated with each data source are jointly learned to capture maximal information, while incorporating pair-wise couplings. With the Lagrangian and its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, the optimization in the dual leads to a generalization of the shifted eigenvalue problem in Lanczos decomposition theorem of KSVD. Further, a covariance-based framework is derived together with using neural networks (NNs) for explicit feature mappings, complementary to the kernel-based interpretation and optimization. Numerical experiments verify the effectiveness of our eKSVD compared to methods based on Mercer kernels for tackling multiple data sources, and our innovation of deploying NNs demonstrates great flexibility for kernel methods.
core_methodology: Extension of Kernel Singular Value Decomposition (KSVD) to multiple data sources (eKSVD) with joint nonlinear feature learning through asymmetric kernels and neural networks for feature mapping
data_sources: Multiple asymmetric data sources suitable for financial applications (e.g., different asset classes, alternative data streams, or cross-market relationships)
alpha_potential: Potential for capturing complex nonlinear relationships between multiple financial data sources (e.g., price, volume, news) that may reveal hidden factors or market regime information
title_cn: 核奇异值分解在多数据源中的扩展
summary_cn: 该研究扩展了核奇异值分解(KSVD)至多数据源场景(eKSVD)，通过联合非线性特征学习和神经网络映射，可应用于金融中多源数据（如不同资产类别）的复杂关系建模，为因子挖掘和市场状态识别提供新方法。

title: Predictively Oriented Gaussian Process Posteriors
summary: Gaussian Processes (GPs) are a powerful tool for modelling and quantifying uncertainty in functional relationships. However, they require practitioners to make a number of design decisions, such as the choice of the kernel and the observation model. Suboptimal choices can produce misspecified models that do not capture the underlying data generating process. We introduce Predictively Oriented Gaussian Processes (PrO-GPs), which treat predictive uncertainty as the primary inferential target and provide a robust alternative to standard GPs. Although direct computation of a PrO posterior for nonparametric models is intractable, we derive a reduced formulation and practical sampling scheme for efficient computation. Through synthetic and real data experiments, we show that PrO-GPs produce better calibrated predictive distributions under model misspecification compared to standard GP approaches.
core_methodology: Predictively Oriented Gaussian Processes (PrO-GPs) that focus on improving predictive uncertainty calibration under model misspecification through a reduced formulation and practical sampling scheme
data_sources: Synthetic and real data (unspecified financial datasets in experiments)
alpha_potential: Potential for improved volatility/uncertainty modeling in options pricing, risk management, or regime-switching detection where standard GPs underperform
title_cn: 面向预测的高斯过程后验
summary_cn: 本文提出的预测导向高斯过程(PrO-GP)通过优化预测不确定性校准，在模型设定错误时比标准GP方法表现更好，可应用于金融市场的波动率建模和风险管理策略。

title: TSGuard: A Real-Time Framework for Detecting and Imputing Missing Data in Streaming Time Series
summary:
Streaming sensor applications routinely suffer from delayed or missing observations caused by faults, communication losses, or environmental interference. Although recent imputation methods exploit temporal and spatial dependencies effectively, most either assume offline access to future observations or prioritize throughput without enforcing domain plausibility. We present TSGuard, a real-time demonstration system for monitoring, validating, and imputing missing values in streaming time series. TSGuard combines a lightweight graph-aware temporal imputation model with constraint-aware validation, fallback estimation, and operator-facing explanations.
  Rather than treating imputation as an isolated prediction task, TSGuard integrates it into a broader data-quality loop: detect problematic observations, impute missing values, validate estimated against physical and spatial constraints, and either retain the original value as a plausible anomaly or replace it when it violates domain constraints. Using environmental sensing as a motivating setting, the demo enables users to inspect delayed sensors, compare imputers, define constraints, and validate flagged values in real time. The combination of lightweight online spatiotemporal imputation, domain-aware validation, and explicit retain-or-replace decisions is our central contribution, while interactive explanations make these decisions inspectable and actionable. for operators.
core_methodology: Lightweight graph-aware temporal imputation model combined with constraint-aware validation and fallback estimation for real-time streaming time series data
data_sources: Streaming time series data from sensors (potentially applicable to market data feeds like tick data, order book updates, or IoT-based alternative data)
alpha_potential: Could improve signal quality in high-frequency trading by ensuring continuous data flow and validating anomalous observations in real-time, particularly valuable for latency-sensitive strategies relying on IoT/alternative data streams
title_cn: TSGuard：一种实时检测和补全流式时间序列缺失数据的框架
summary_cn: TSGuard独创性地将轻量级时空补全与领域约束验证相结合，为金融实时数据流（如高频行情）提供异常检测-补全-验证闭环处理。其在线学习架构和保留/替换决策机制可有效提升交易信号可靠性，特别适合对数据连续性要求严苛的量化策略。

title: Learn Feasibility Once, Optimize All Objectives: Derivative-Free Diffusion Models for Chance-Constrained Programming
summary: Chance-constrained programs (CCPs) optimize decisions under uncertainty by limiting the probability of constraint violation. Despite advances in traditional and learning-based approaches, optimizing non-convex or non-smooth objectives and adapting to different objectives under fixed chance constraints remain challenging. In this paper, we propose a \textbf{D}erivative-free \textbf{D}iffusion-based framework that \textbf{D}isentangles constraint modeling from objective optimization, termed \textbf{D$^3$Opt}. We learn the chance-feasible structure once, independently of any particular objective, by training a risk-conditioned diffusion model solely on constraint-filtered decisions and freezing it as a reusable prior for post-specified objectives. At inference time, we propose an annealed, particle-based Feynman--Kac correction along the frozen reverse diffusion process to optimize post-specified objectives using only function evaluations. This enables derivative-free optimization of non-convex and non-smooth objectives without objective-specific retraining. We prove that the correction preserves feasibility when this property holds for the frozen prior, and derive an optimization-error bound separating learned-prior coverage, finite-particle approximation, and finite-temperature effects. Experiments on linear Gaussian CCPs, objective-transfer tasks, and chance-constrained economic dispatch demonstrate effective optimization across smooth and non-smooth objectives, including non-convex cases, and objective generalization under fixed chance constraints without retraining.
core_methodology: Derivative-free Diffusion-based framework (D$^3$Opt) that disentangles constraint modeling from objective optimization, using a risk-conditioned diffusion model for chance-constrained programming.
data_sources: Experiments on linear Gaussian CCPs, objective-transfer tasks, and chance-constrained economic dispatch.
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing non-convex and non-smooth objectives in portfolio optimization under uncertainty without retraining for different objectives.

title: Learning Transferable Policies from Action-free Time Series Through Dynamical Embeddings
summary: Learning control from action-free recordings is challenging because intervention effects are unobserved and policies may exploit errors in reconstructed dynamics.
